title: Suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage
keyNumbers: Noncontrast head CT: <6 h from onset, no new deficit, high-quality scanner read by neuroradiology: sensitivity ~98.7%
Presentation >6 h, or new neurological deficit: CT; if negative, LP
Ottawa SAH Rule: further testing if any of age ≥40, neck pain/stiffness, witnessed LOC, onset with exertion, thunderclap (instant peak), limited neck flexion
Secure the aneurysm early, preferably within 24 h (AHA 2023 key message)
No routine seizure prophylaxis (consider in high-risk patients); avoid phenytoin; new seizures → ASM for 7 days (AHA 2023 key message)
consultQuestion: Sudden severe headache — rule out SAH? CT negative, need LP?
keyHistory: Prior sentinel headache in recent weeks
Family history of aneurysm/SAH, polycystic kidney disease

clues: Blood anterior to the midbrain/pons only, good grade
Recurrent thunderclap headaches, convexity SAH, segmental vasoconstriction
Older, transient focal spells, superficial siderosis
Diagnosis of exclusion after negative workup

notes: <6 h from onset, no new deficit, high-quality scanner read by neuroradiology: sensitivity ~98.7%

workup.test: LP: opening pressure, cell counts in tubes 1 and 4, xanthochromia (spectrophotometry if available)
indication: CT negative and presentation >6 h from onset or new neurological deficit
notes: Often done >6–12 h after onset; xanthochromia sensitivity 100%, specificity 95.2% (pooled)

workup.test: Imaging for other thunderclap causes: CTA/MRA head and neck, CT/MR venography, MRI brain — see thunderclap-headache
indication: Features of cervical artery dissection, RCVS, CVT or pituitary apoplexy
Diffuse SAH with negative or inconclusive CTA

decisionRules.recommendation: Prompt workup to diagnose or exclude aSAH

decisionRules.condition: Alert, >15 y, severe nontraumatic headache peaking within 1 h
decisionRules.recommendation: Ottawa SAH Rule: further testing if any of age ≥40, neck pain/stiffness, witnessed LOC, onset with exertion, thunderclap (instant peak), limited neck flexion
Negative high-quality CT read by neuroradiology is reasonable to exclude aSAH

decisionRules.condition: Presentation >6 h, or new neurological deficit
Spontaneous SAH with high concern for aneurysm, CTA negative or inconclusive

decisionRules.recommendation: Grade with Hunt-Hess or WFNS for severity and prognosis

decisionRules.condition: Confirmed aSAH at a low-volume hospital
decisionRules.recommendation: Timely transfer to a high-volume center with neurocritical care and cerebrovascular/endovascular expertise

initialSteps: Secure the aneurysm early, preferably within 24 h (AHA 2023 key message)
Enteral nimodipine early (AHA 2023 key message); routine antifibrinolytics don't improve outcome
No routine seizure prophylaxis (consider in high-risk patients); avoid phenytoin; new seizures → ASM for 7 days (AHA 2023 key message)
disposition: Confirmed aSAH: neuro ICU at a high-volume center
Negative CT + LP: consider other thunderclap causes
institutionVaries: Spectrophotometric xanthochromia availability vs visual inspection
CTA-first vs LP-first for CT-negative patients (no head-to-head data; AHA 2023)
pearls: Negative CT within 6 h may miss <1.5 per 1000 SAH — but this doesn't apply to atypical presentations (neck pain, syncope, seizure, focal deficit) (AHA 2023)
Perimesencephalic SAH: CTA alone vs DSA is in equipoise (AHA 2023)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436
